title: Add draining state for graceful Dag pausing
body: Pausing a Dag today is abrupt: it stops the Dag mid-flight, letting running tasks finish but stranding queued and downstream tasks until it is unpaused. There is no way to say "stop starting new scheduled runs, but let the work in flight finish." That gap bites hardest during upgrades and maintenance windows. The workaround in the wild is to rewrite every Dag's schedule to `None`, wait for runs to drain, do the work, then put the schedules back — invasive, and easy to get wrong. This adds a `draining` scheduling state that expresses it directly: - **Draining** blocks new scheduler-created Dag runs, including scheduled and asset-triggered runs, while letting task instances in queued and running runs continue to be scheduled. - Explicit triggers remain available while draining, matching paused-Dag behavior. A manual, operator-triggered, asset-materialization, or backfill request extends the drain until the resulting work finishes. - The scheduler moves a draining Dag to `paused` once no unfinished runs remain and no newly accepted backfill is still initializing, recording a `drain_completed` audit log entry. **Draining is transient, not a third resting state.** It always converges to `paused`; the resting states are still `active` and `paused`. The UI reflects that — the pause control stays a binary toggle, and drain is offered at the one moment it carries meaning: flipping a Dag off while it still has unfinished runs asks whether to *drain then pause* or *pause now*. A Dag with nothing running pauses in a single click as before, since the two are equivalent there. **API.** `DAGResponse` gains a `scheduling_state` field. `PATCH /dags/{dag_id}` accepts either `is_paused` or `scheduling_state` and rejects a body carrying both. Existing `is_paused` clients are unaffected. **Migration.** Adds `dag.is_draining` (non-null, default false) with an index and a `NOT (is_paused AND is_draining)` check constraint. It also adds a supporting index for identifying an initializing backfill by Dag. closes: #22006 Screenshots: --- ##### Was generative AI tooling used to co-author this PR? - [X] Yes — Codex (GPT-5) and Claude Code (Opus 5) Generated-by: Codex (GPT-5), Claude Code (Opus 5) following [the guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#gen-ai-assisted-contributions)
